body: [{"streamId":"01a0d8d1-14e0-7422-8281-a1821629bc9d","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0d8d1-14e0-7422-8281-a1821629bc9d\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022Root cause is written into the fix\\u0027s own commit and the pull request description: the Project aggregate\\u0027s team-facing events are merged onto the receiver\\u0027s own local Project stream, where the ordinary outbox lands post-switch-on events first and the catch-up answer serves the older head afterward, so the per-origin high-water guard in EventReplicationInbox, keyed on that receiver-local stream, refuses the head as out of order on every reconcile and nothing can repair it\u0022,\u0022The origin high-water refusal in EventReplicationInbox no longer applies to events ProjectStreamReplicationRules.IsProjectAggregateStreamEvent names; it applies unchanged to every other stream, the existing out-of-order refusal test for a Task stream still passes, and a duplicate of an already-applied origin event id is still dropped for those events by the existing idempotency check\u0022,\u0022For exactly those events, the ProjectDetails projection gives the same answer whatever order they arrive in: a member vouch or removal is last-writer per fingerprint by the event\\u0027s own IssuedAt, so a removal stamped later than a vouch wins even when the vouch arrives second; a team-settings change is applied per changed field only when that field\\u0027s ChangedAt is not older than the one already applied; a prompt-addendum or run-skill change is applied only when its own issued time is not older than the one already applied; so a pre-switch-on head arriving after a newer tail never overwrites a newer value\u0022,\u0022A two-store test reproduces the issue\\u0027s shape: origin A holds a MemberVouched and a ProjectTeamSettingsChanged before its switch-on point and another ProjectTeamSettingsChanged after it; receiver B takes the ordinary post-switch-on flush first, then the bootstrap catch-up answer (the path a fresh join runs). The test fails on the current tip and passes with the fix, and proves B\\u0027s ProjectDetails.Members holds the vouched member, its team settings match A\\u0027s newest, ProjectJoinStatus.NotJoined reads false, and the log carries no out-of-order refusal for those events\u0022,\u0022A node already stuck in this state on v0.10.50 is repaired by the daemon\\u0027s own next catch-up with no hand steps, and by an explicit h9k project reconcile \\u003Cproject\\u003E run before that; proven by the same two-store test starting from a store that already holds the refused tail and no head\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Type\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Model\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RevisedAt\u0022:\u00222026-09-26T15:51:45.872459\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022RevisedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022QueuePriority\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022ClearInteractiveMode\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022CloseLinkedIssue\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Constraints\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false}}","originEventId":"1f3cf08c-1483-4be4-844c-0a3af62e3dc3","originSequence":65669,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-09-26T15:51:45.882151+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"}]
